Definition: Understandability refers to how easily developers can comprehend and maintain the test code.

Task: Improve the understandability of the test `GroupedRandomAccessSource_ESTest_test8.java` (path:- /Users/tenghaha/Projects/New_Agent_understandability_improvement/data/original/itextpdf/auto/testcases/GroupedRandomAccessSource_ESTest/GroupedRandomAccessSource_ESTest_test8.java). The refactored code must be syntactically correct and compilable against the provided CUT signatures. Do not alter the runtime behaviour of the original test: the same methods must be called with the same arguments and produce the same expected outcomes.

The compile failure is environmental, not a problem with the test code: `javac` is rejecting `--release 5` (the configured source level) because the installed JDK no longer supports release 5. This happens before any symbol resolution and is unrelated to my refactoring — the original test would fail the same way under this JDK. The refactored test itself is syntactically correct and uses the same API calls and arguments as the original.

The improved test renames the method to describe the behavior (`readPastDestinationBufferBoundsThrowsArrayIndexOutOfBounds`), uses meaningful variable names, and documents why the exception is expected — while preserving identical runtime behavior (`groupedSource.get(5L, sixByteBuffer, 5, 5)` expecting an `ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException` from `ArrayRandomAccessSource`).
